name: Denver
operatingHours: Light rail and the A Line run ~3:30–4:30 AM to ~1:00–1:30 AM daily; there is no overnight rail service. The A Line runs every 15 min most of the day (~30 min early and late); light rail lines run every 15–30 min.
fareInfo: One flat local fare: a $2.75 3-Hour Pass covers any light rail or bus trip with unlimited transfers for 3 hours; a Day Pass is $5.50 (2026). Trips to or from Denver Airport need the $10 Airport Day Pass, valid systemwide all day. Pay by tapping a contactless bank card or phone (fares cap automatically to day/month passes), in the RTD MyRide/NextRide app, or at station ticket machines. Riders 19 and under ride free.

sights.name: Denver Botanic Gardens
sights.note: Twenty-four acres of themed gardens beside Cheesman Park, from a Japanese garden to high-plains and alpine plantings and a domed tropical conservatory.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–4:00 PM to Nov 18; 9:00 AM–2:30 PM Nov 19–Dec 31 (holiday lights in the evening are separately ticketed); 9:00 AM–8:00 PM in summer

sights.name: Denver Union Station
sights.note: The restored 1914 Beaux-Arts rail terminal, now a hotel, bar and food hall around a grand waiting room and the hub for the A Line and light rail.
sights.hours: Great Hall open daily from early morning to late night; shops and bars keep their own hours

sights.name: Denver Museum of Nature & Science
sights.note: Dinosaurs, gems, Egyptian mummies, a planetarium and an IMAX screen in City Park, with a classic skyline-and-mountain view from the back steps.

sights.name: Coors Field
sights.note: Home of the Colorado Rockies in LoDo, with a row of purple seats marking exactly one mile above sea level.
sights.hours: Rockies home games ~Apr–Sep; guided ballpark tours run most days year-round

sights.name: Molly Brown House Museum
sights.note: The Victorian home of Titanic survivor Margaret 'Molly' Brown, seen on a 45-minute guided tour of period rooms.
sights.hours: Wed–Sun 10:00 AM–5:00 PM (Thu to 7:00 PM), last entry 1 hour before close; closed Mon–Tue

sights.name: Denver Art Museum
sights.note: Two striking buildings, one a titanium-clad Libeskind design, holding major Indigenous American, Western and modern collections.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Tue to 8:00 PM; closed Wed

sights.name: Denver Zoo
sights.note: An 80-acre zoo in City Park known for its Asian Tropics elephant habitat and big-cat, primate and bear areas.
sights.hours: Open daily, ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM in the warm months and ~10:00 AM–4:00 PM in winter

sights.name: Downtown Aquarium
sights.note: A riverside aquarium with tiger and shark exhibits and a restaurant built around a huge tank.
sights.hours: Mon–Thu & Sun 10:00 AM–8:00 PM, Fri–Sat 10:00 AM–9:00 PM

sights.name: Wings Over the Rockies Air & Space Museum
sights.note: Historic military jets, a B-52 and space exhibits inside a 1930s hangar at the former Lowry Air Force Base.

sights.name: Empower Field at Mile High
sights.note: The Denver Broncos' stadium beside the light rail, with a team hall of fame and behind-the-scenes stadium tours.
sights.hours: Broncos home games ~Sep–Jan; stadium tours on most non-event days

sights.name: United States Mint at Denver
sights.note: A free hour-long tour of the 1906 mint, where most U.S. circulating coins carrying a 'D' mark are struck.
sights.hours: Free tours Mon–Thu at 7:15, 8:30, 9:45, 11:30 AM, 12:45 & 2:00 PM; online reservation required (up to 30 days ahead); ages 7+

sights.name: Forney Museum of Transportation
sights.note: A sprawling hall of vintage cars, carriages and locomotives, including the giant Union Pacific 'Big Boy' steam engine.

sights.name: Meow Wolf's Convergence Station
sights.note: A four-storey walk-through immersive art installation of neon worlds, hidden passages and a puzzle-like storyline.
sights.hours: Hours vary by day; entry only at your ticketed time

sights.name: Larimer Square
sights.note: Denver's oldest block, a strip of Victorian storefronts with restaurants and bars under strings of overhead lights.
sights.hours: Open-air street, always open; shops and restaurants keep their own hours

sights.name: Colorado State Capitol
sights.note: The gold-domed statehouse, with a step marked one mile high and a free guided tour that climbs to the dome.
sights.hours: Mon–Fri 7:30 AM–5:00 PM; free tours on the hour 10:00 AM–3:00 PM (dome on tours only); closed weekends

sights.name: Washington Park
sights.note: A favourite local park with two lakes, flower gardens and a loop path popular with runners and cyclists.

sights.name: Denver Central Market
sights.note: A food hall in a converted RiNo warehouse with stalls for pizza, tacos, pastries, coffee and a central bar.

sights.name: RiNo Art District
sights.note: Former warehouse streets in River North covered with large murals, plus breweries and galleries along Larimer and Walnut.
sights.hours: Outdoor murals always viewable; galleries and bars keep their own hours

railStations.name: Denver Union Station
railStations.note: Amtrak's California Zephyr (Chicago–San Francisco Bay Area) stops daily, plus the seasonal Winter Park Express ski train. Downtown's transit hub: the A Line to the airport, the B/G/N commuter lines and the E and W light rail lines all stop here, with the free MallRide bus along 16th Street.
railStations.hours: Station open daily from early morning to late night; trains from ~3:30 AM to ~1:30 AM. Amtrak runs to its own timetable.

airports.name: Denver International Airport
airports.transitNote: The RTD A Line commuter train (shown on map) leaves from the south side of the Jeppesen Terminal, under the Westin hotel, and reaches Denver Union Station in ~37 min; the $10 Airport Day Pass applies.
airports.hours: A Line: first ~4:00 AM, last ~1:00 AM from the airport; every 15 min most of the day, ~30 min early and late.
